body.answer:

Sources: [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-ARTS) [15](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

question: what classes do you need for the biology major

body.answer:
The catalog lists the Biology BS (Bachelor of Science); Biology Minor is also published. [15]

Required major courses: BIOL 111 & 111L; BIOL 113 & 113L; BIOL 332 & 332L; BIOL 356; BIOL 407 & 407L; CHEM 117 & 117L; PHYS 111 & 118L; PHYS 113 & 119L. Organic chemistry: choose one option—CHEM 206 & 206L, or CHEM 211 & 211L plus CHEM 213 & 213L. Ecology: choose BIOL 221 or ENSC 220. Math: choose 2—CMPS 147, BIOL 354 or PSYC 242, MATH 110, 121 or 122. [1]

Choose 4 electives, including at least 1 with lab/field and at least 1 without lab/field. Lab/field options: BIOL 214/214L & 216/216L; 311/311L; 320; 324; 328/328L; 349; 410/410L; 420; 430; ENSC 220/220L, 320 or 417/417L. No-lab/field options: BIIN 350, 351; BIOL 204, 304, 335, 343, 345, 346, 347, 354, 357, 390; CHEM 425; GEOG 309; ENSC 320. Also required: PATH 001, 002 and 003. [1]

BIOL 113 is 4 credits; BIOL 113L is 1 credit. Each requires BIOL 110, or BIOL 111 and 111L; take BIOL 113L concurrently with 113 and 113 concurrently with 113L. [2][3]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-BIOL) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/BIOL113L) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/BIOL113) [15](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

question: does ramapo have anything like scientific illustration or a major that combines art and science

body.answer:
Ramapo lists no Scientific Illustration major in its catalog. It does offer COMM 224 FUNDAMENTALS OF ILLUSTRATION (4 credits; no published prerequisites). The catalog describes it as investigating “illustration’s capacity for personal expression within the arena of public communication,” including picture building, conceptual development, materials, and professional sharing and feedback. COMM 224 is not listed in the Visual Arts BA requirements. [2][1][5]

The catalog lists a Visual Arts BA and an Interdisciplinary Studies BA, but no specifically named art-and-science major. [5] A related option is the Visual Arts BA’s joint Art Therapy degree option: students complete the BA at Ramapo, then continue at Caldwell University for an MA in Counseling with Mental Health Counseling/Art Therapy Specialization. It combines visual arts with psychology coursework, rather than being a scientific-illustration program. [1][7]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-ARTS) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/COMM224) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/freshmen/admission-requirements/)

question: does an art class count for gen ed or do i need a specific category

body.answer:
You need a course approved for a specific General Education category; being an art class alone does not establish that it counts. The pages say to choose two of the three distribution categories, and to check the catalog’s approved General Education courses. [6][7][8]
Examples of art courses with Gen Ed attributes in the catalog: ARTS 206 BLACK AND WHITE PHOTOGRAPHY, ARTS 209 3D MODELING AND ANIMATION, and ARTS 214 BASIC CERAMICS are Culture & Creativity; ARTS 217 LOCAL TO GLOBAL: WORLD ANIMATION NOW and ARTS 230 REVOLUTION & LIGHT: THE ROOTS OF HAITIAN ART are Global Awareness; ARTS 219 ART AND INTERACTION is Values and Ethics. [3]
The curriculum page says take one course in two of three distribution categories: Culture & Creativity, Systems, Sustainability, & Society, and Values & Ethics; at least one must be offered by a school other than the one housing your major. [8] See the approved courses in the catalog: https://catalog.ramapo.edu/college-wide-programs/gened#general-education-categories-and-courses. [7]

Sources: [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/)

question: what are the gen ed requirements i need to finish regardless of major

body.answer:
Ramapo students complete ten General Education courses: four keystone courses, one course in each of four keystone categories, and one course in two of three distribution categories. [3]

Keystone courses: First Year Seminar, Social Science Inquiry, Critical Reading & Writing 102, and Studies in the Arts & Humanities. Critical Reading & Writing 102 must be taken within the first 64 credits. [3] Another catalog page calls this course Critical Reading and Writing II. [4][9] It says reading and writing, as well as mathematics, must be completed by 64 earned credits; Banner blocks registration until Critical Reading and Writing II and general education mathematics are completed. [9]

Keystone categories: Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning. Quantitative Reasoning must be taken within the first 64 credits. [3]

Distribution: take one course in two of three categories. Page [3] lists Culture & Creativity, Systems, Sustainability, & Society, and Values & Ethics; page [6] lists Culture and Creativity, Values and Ethics, and Social Systems and Society, so the pages differ in the category names. Page [3] says at least one course must be offered by a school other than the one housing your major. Page [6] says that starting Fall 2026, the “out of school requirement” is no longer enforced in degree audit tools. [3][6]

Approved General Education courses: https://catalog.ramapo.edu/college-wide-programs/gened#general-education-categories-and-courses [8]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [9](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education-reading-writing-and-mathematics)

question: if i want to do bio what should i take freshman year so i dont fall behind

If you’re admitted to Biology for the 2026–2027 academic year, the recommended Biology (General) plan is [1]:

**First Year, Fall (18 credits):** BIOL 111 & BIOL 111L (4); CHEM 116 & CHEM 116L (4); CRWT 102 (4); INTD 101 (4).

**First Year, Spring (18 credits):** BIOL 113 & BIOL 113L (4); CHEM 117 & CHEM 117L (4); one Quantitative Reasoning option: MATH 110, MATH 121, or CMPS 147 (4; CMPS 147 is strongly recommended); one General Education Requirement (4); PATH 001 (no credits listed).

The plan is applicable to students admitted into the major during 2026–2027. [1]

question: can a lab science class count for both gen ed and a minor at the same time

body.answer:

question: I work full time and want to go back for a business degree. What are the required courses for the Business Administration major, and how many credits is the major in total?

body.answer:
The catalog lists no bachelor's major in Business Administration; it lists the Business Administration MBA (Master of Business Administration). It also lists Healthcare Administration BS and International Business BA as bachelor's majors. [14]

For the MBA:
- The 30-credit Advanced Standing Program requires 7 core courses and 3 electives. Core courses: MBAD 601 Accounting for Managerial Decision Making; MBAD 610 Becoming a 21st Century Leader; MBAD 620 Financial Management I; MBAD 638 Info Tech for Managers; MBAD 640 Marketing Management & Strategy; MBAD 660 Operations Management; MBAD 675 MBA IFK Assessment; MBAD 680 Managing Responsible Global Business. Choose 3 electives (9 credits) from the catalog's elective list. [1]
- The 42-credit Program adds 6 foundational courses (2 credits each): ACCT 510 Foundations of Accounting; BADM 510 Foundation Stats for Business; ECON 510 Foundations of Economics; FINC 510 Foundations of Finance; MGMT 510 Foundations of Management; MKTG 510 Foundations of Marketing. It also requires the 30 credits of core courses and electives above. Students in the 30-credit Advanced Standing Program do not need the foundational-course requirement. [1]

The catalog's elective list is lengthy; see https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-MBA-MBAD for all options. [1] For the MBA's total credits, the catalog says 30 credits for Advanced Standing or 42 credits for the other program. [1] Undergraduate major requirements are 40–64 credits, but that rule applies to undergraduate students, not this MBA. [2]

Contact the Anisfield School of Business at asb@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7379, (201) 684-7380, or (201) 684-7378. [1]

question: How many gen ed credits does a bachelors at Ramapo require in total, and what are the categories I have to cover?

body.answer:
The pages do not give a fixed total number of Gen Ed credits. They say the curriculum “should not exceed 41 credits” [7]. Ramapo students take ten Gen Ed courses: four keystone courses, one course in each of four keystone categories, and one course in two of three distribution categories [10].

The four keystone courses are First Year Seminar, Social Science Inquiry, Critical Reading & Writing 102, and Studies in the Arts & Humanities. Take Critical Reading & Writing 102 within your first 64 credits [10]. The four keystone categories are Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning; Quantitative Reasoning must also be completed within the first 64 credits [10].

Choose two of these distribution categories: Culture & Creativity, Values and Ethics, and the third category. The pages differ on its name: “Systems, Sustainability, & Society” [9, 10] versus “Social Systems and Society” [11]. Section 10 says at least one distribution course must be offered by a school other than your major’s school; the Fall 2026 page says the “out of school requirement” is no longer enforced in degree audit tools [10, 11].

For clarification, contact the Office of the Provost: provost@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7330 [6].

Sources: [6](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education) [7](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/)

question: Is there a certificate program in data analytics or project management that someone could do part time?

body.answer:
The catalog lists no certificate for “data analytics.” It names two related graduate certificates: Data Analyst-Graduate Certificate and Data Modeler-Graduate Certificate. [17] It lists BADM 501 DATA ANALYTICS as a course (3 credits; no published prerequisites), not as a certificate. [2]

The listed project management options are courses, not evidence of a certificate: MBAD 664 PROJECT MANAGEMENT (3 credits; no published prerequisites) [3], and MGMT 472 PROJECT MANAGEMENT (4 credits; prerequisite: MGMT 370 OPERATIONS MANAGEMENT). [4] I don’t have verified information about a project management certificate or whether either certificate can be completed part time.

For certificate questions, contact the Office of the Provost: provost@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7330. Its pages describe academic and professional certificates but don’t establish part-time availability. [5][6][7]

Sources: [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/BADM501) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/MBAD664) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/MGMT472) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#certificate-programs1) [6](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#certificate-programs1) [7](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#certificate-programs1) [17](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

question: Can you check my transcript from county college and tell me which of my credits will transfer into the business major?

body.answer:
I can’t check your personal transcript or determine which of your credits will transfer. Ramapo says transfer students’ transcripts are reviewed by Admissions, and specific application of accepted credits to course requirements must be approved through transfer evaluation and advisement [10].

For New Jersey community-college credits, use www.NJTransfer.org for course equivalencies and academic planning [2][5]. If you have an A.A. or A.S. from a New Jersey community college, Ramapo accepts the full degree up to the two-year-school maximum of 65 transfer credits; A.A.S. degrees and credits without an associate degree are evaluated course by course [2].

After acceptance, you receive a Transfer Credit Worksheet showing accepted credits. Coursework needing review may be submitted to the major Convener or reviewed at orientation for detailed course equivalency [4]. Admissions: admissions@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7300, McBride House [2].

The catalog lists International Business BA as the bachelor's business major [12]. Its published requirements list courses, but no total credit count [1].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-BA-IBUS) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/faqs/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/faqs/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/agreements/) [10](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#transferring-academic-credit1) [12](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

question: whats the difference between the computer science major and the information technology major in terms of required classes? i dont want a lot of heavy math if i can avoid it

body.answer:
The catalog lists Computer Science BS, a Bachelor of Science major [15]. Its required courses are CMPS 147 Computer Science I; 148 Computer Science II; 220 Assembly Language Programming; 231 Data Structures; 311 Operating Systems; 361 Software Design; 366 Organization of Programming Languages; 450 Senior Project; MATH 121 Calculus I; and MATH 205 Mathematical Structures or MATH 237 Discrete Structures. It also requires 2 math electives (from MATH 122, 124, 200, 225, 240, 245, 253, 262, 282, 290, 300, 305, 321, 339, 353 or 370, 360, or 390), 7 computer science electives (CMPS 240 or 285, 305, 310, 315, 320, 327, 331, 335, 337, 342, 345, 350, 357, 364, 367, 369, 370, 373, 375, or DATA 301), and PATH 001, 002, and 003 [1]. The IT page provided describes the field but gives no required classes [9], so I can’t verify an IT-vs-CS course comparison or which has less math. CS does require calculus, mathematical/discrete structures, and two math electives [1].

For IT requirements, contact the School of Science, Nursing, and Health Office: SNHOffice@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7734, ASB-422.

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-CMPS) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/study-abroad/academic-search/information-technology/) [15](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

question: Does a statistics course like MATH 108 satisfy the quantitative reasoning gen ed, and is it required for the business admin major?

body.answer:
Yes. MATH 108 carries the Gen Ed attribute “Gen Ed 18-Quantitative Rsng (GEQR)” [4]. It is one of the catalog courses with that attribute; the catalog also lists MATH 100T, 101, 104, 106, and 110 [17]. Quantitative Reasoning is a required General Education category, which must be completed within the first 64 credits [6].

The catalog lists no bachelor’s major called “business admin”; it lists Healthcare Administration BS and International Business BA as bachelor’s majors named for part of it, and Business Administration MBA [17]. MATH 108 is not listed in the Business Administration MBA requirements [1]. So the catalog does not establish that MATH 108 is required for a “business admin” major. The course is 4 credits and has stated prerequisites [4].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-MBA-MBAD) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/MATH108) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [17](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

question: Are there any evening sections of intro accounting open for spring? I can only take classes after 6pm

body.answer:
The Registrar lists the Spring 2027 Schedule of Classes as available to view [4], but I don’t have verified information about whether an Intro Accounting section after 6 p.m. is currently open. Use the [Schedule of Classes](https://myssb.ramapo.edu/StudentRegistrationSsb/ssb/term/termSelection?mode=search): select “Class Schedules” and search Spring 2027; narrow by subject, course number or title, then filter by start and end times [2].

Contact the Registrar at reg@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7695 to ask about current openings [2, 4].

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/instructions-how-to-use-class-schedule-course-description-search/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/)

question: What concentrations are offered within the business administration major, and how many credits is each concentration?

body.answer:
The catalog lists no bachelor’s major named “Business Administration.” It lists Healthcare Administration BS and International Business BA as bachelor’s majors named for part of it, and Business Administration MBA. [13] The MBA is described as a 30-credit Advanced Standing Program or a 42-credit Program; these are MBA program totals, not concentration credits. [1] The pages don’t provide concentrations or credit totals for each concentration. For help, contact the Anisfield School of Business at asb@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7379. [13]

question: Honestly which would be a better fit for me as a 34 yr old working adult, nursing or computing? I'm worried about the clinical hours

body.answer:
I can’t determine which is a better personal fit, and the pages don’t give clinical-hour schedules or computing-program details. The ABSN is described as a “full-time, daytime, in-person intensive experience.” [1] The generic BSN has two years of general education and science requirements, followed by a two-year nursing sequence. [2] Neither description specifies clinical hours. The pages therefore don’t establish whether either schedule fits around your work. [1][2]

To explore your choice, Ramapo’s Cahill Career Development Center offers FOCUS 2 to help students select a major; use access code “ramapo430.” [10] You can also visit a Career Advisor for assessment information. [11] The Center for Student Success recommends gathering information, using career-center assessments, and talking with faculty in majors you’re considering. [13]

For clinical scheduling details, contact the Nursing Programs Office at (201) 684-7749. For career guidance, contact the Cahill Career Development Center at careercenter@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7444. [10][11]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURA) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURG) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/careercenter/career-assessment/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/careercenter/career-assessment/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/major/)
